newsitem.title: USA: Lobbyist's lawyers to ask for dismissal of charges.
newsitem.headline: Lobbyist's lawyers to ask for dismissal of charges.

text.p: Defense attorneys said they would ask for dismissal Thursday of charges against lobbyist Jack Williams, accused of false statements in an investigation of former Department of Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy.
Williams stood accused of two criminal counts of making false statements to investigators.
"We don't expect to be convicted," said John Kotelly, a member of Williams' defense team.
The motion for a directed verdict was to be argued early in the afternoon. Prosecutors completed their case at midday.
Maximum penalty for Williams would be five years in prison and a $250,000 fine.
Espy resigned in 1994 amid allegations he improperly accepted gifts from firms regulated by his department.
Williams was Washington lobbyist for Tyson Foods Inc, a major U.S. meatpacker, when Espy was a Tyson guest at a pro football game in Dallas on January 16, 1994.
Investigators for USDA and the FBI said Williams told them he knew nothing about Espy's trip and did not even know the phone number for Patricia Dempsey, Espy's girlfriend.

However, other witnesses said Williams paid for Dempsey's airline ticket to Dallas and told Tyson headquarters when she would arrive. Williams also passed on a Tyson Foundation scholarship application to Dempsey.
Barry Levine, Williams' other attorney, has described the trial as an attempt by prosecutors to coerce Williams into providing harmful information about Espy.
